label: Mike Rounds
narrative: Rounds is the Republican half of the UAPDA and, unlike Schumer, he has never stopped filing it. He was an original cosponsor of S.Amdt. 797 on 13 July 2023. When the provision was gutted in conference he took over as lead sponsor: on 11 July 2024 the full text, eminent domain clause intact, was submitted to the FY2025 NDAA as S.Amdt. 2610, captioned 'Mr. ROUNDS (for himself and Mr. Schumer),' and printed in the Congressional Record for that day. It was ordered to lie on the table and was never called up; the FY2025 NDAA, P.L. 118-159, signed 23 December 2024, contains no UAP disclosure division at all. Rounds sits on both the Armed Services and Intelligence Committees, the two panels that would have to be rolled to move this, and his position on the inside is what makes his persistence significant rather than symbolic. As of 2026 he is still at it: in his own newsletter for the week of 22-28 June 2026 he wrote, 'On Thursday, I spoke at the 2026 Disclosure Symposium, where I discussed the future of the Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (UAP) Disclosure Act. I am once again cosponsoring as an amendment to this year's National Defense Authorization Act.' That FY2027 NDAA, S. 4784, was reported by the Armed Services Committee in June 2026 containing no UAP provisions of any kind, which means the vehicle Rounds is aiming at has again been built without a place for him.
